title: GCC recovery tracker shows worsening conditions
author: Keith Mason
text:
RESEARCH BRIEFING

26 Nov 2026

GCC recovery tracker shows worsening conditions

GCC recovery faces challenges with declining economic indicators and regional
tensions, yet growth is still anticipated in the coming months.

GCC recovery conditions have deteriorated significantly, with the recovery tracker index dropping by 15 points to 36.6 in October, its lowest since March. This decline aligns with a revised growth forecast of 4.6% for next year, 0.9 percentage points lower than previously anticipated.

The index’s downturn is attributed to rising bond spreads, falling equity
prices, and disruptions in flight arrivals, particularly following attacks on
Saudi Arabia’s infrastructure. Although Saudi oil production increased by 11.9%
to 10 million barrels per day, the overall recovery remains fragile, with trade
and energy flows at risk from potential conflict escalation.

All GCC economies experienced some decline in October, with Oman facing the
largest drop. Despite this, growth is still expected in Q4, supported by oil
production levels. While most regional PMIs eased, they remained in expansionary
territory, indicating some resilience in the economic landscape.
